_about: Model registry. Each entry maps a row of Table 3 in Raihan et al. (JIIS 2025) to an exact Hugging Face repo and a pinned commit (revision), so every run uses byte-identical weights, tokenizer and chat template. The paper gives only name, size and 'version', not HF ids or base-vs-instruct. Choices and reasons below; confirm with Nishat. 'primary' = the replication run; 'sensitivity' = alternative reading of the paper, run to see which reading reproduces the paper's numbers. Revisions pinned 2026-09-29 from the Hugging Face API.

llama31_8b_instruct.gated: manual: request access to Llama 3.1 on huggingface.co with your account, then `hf auth login` on Hopper
llama31_8b_instruct.why: 'Version 3.1' plus the Dubey et al. (2024) citation, which is the Llama 3.1 ('Llama 3 Herd') paper. Instruct, not base, because the paper's prompt is a chat prompt with a system part ('You are a helpful AI assistant...'). The paper calls Llama/Mistral 'base models', but its v1 README also labels GPT-3.5 'Base', so there 'base' means general-purpose (not code-tuned), not pretrained-only.

mistral_7b_instruct_v01.why: 'Version 0.1' plus the Mistral 7B paper (Jiang et al., 2023). Instruct for the same reason as Llama. The chat template at this revision (updated 2025-07-24) accepts a system message by prepending it to the first user turn; earlier template versions rejected system messages.

llama31_8b_base.paper_row: Llama-3 | Open | 8B | Version 3.1 (alternative reading: pretrained base model)
llama31_8b_base.gated: manual (same Llama 3.1 access as the instruct model)
llama31_8b_base.why: Sensitivity check for the base-vs-instruct ambiguity. Base models get the paper's three prompt parts as plain text.

mistral_7b_base_v01.paper_row: Mistral | Open | 7B | Version 0.1 (alternative reading: pretrained base model)
mistral_7b_base_v01.why: Sensitivity check for the base-vs-instruct ambiguity (no chat template; plain-text prompt).
